why: Each window kept its own Superhot dial, and the state word (sa) tells the host that a window with the dial off is always acting, so with player 1 on and player 2 off time never stopped for anyone. The host now sends its dial in the world word twice a second (netWorldSend, beside kid mode) and a linked window puts it on its live dial CFG.superhot, which the time gate, the state word, the Settings row and the backquote line all read; its saved word (P.gameOpts) is never written, the live value it replaced (NET.shOwn) is put back on netReset, applyGameOpts keeps the host value on top after any other row click, and the row and the key on a linked window say the host sets it instead of moving. On the run card every extraction timer (beacon countdown, the landed window and shipHold, G.timeLeft, the wave clock) already takes the frame dt after the Superhot gate, on host and guest alike, so they obey it; two paths did not. The kept raid a spectating host runs (netSpecTick) ticked its clock and world with raw dt and sent that clock to the party, and a window paused in a shared raid skipped the gate entirely (it required !G.paused) while the world ran on, so its clock and rings ran and were snapped back by the host word every half second. Both now stand still unless a teammate up top is acting, by the same netAnyActing rule of v16.27.
